title: Awareness without acceptance and distress: tests on two open datasets (Antunes et al., Zenodo 14946661; Ireland, Zenodo 19701724)

claims.statement: In this sample (n = 114), mindful acceptance, not awareness, carries the association with distress (DASS-21 total: r = -0.42 vs -0.06), and there is no 'awareness without acceptance' penalty: the awareness x acceptance interaction is small, non-significant and of the opposite sign (std beta +0.08, p = .30; anxiety +0.16, p = .058).
claims.scope: Cross-sectional, one sample of adults (ages ~20-49 in the rows inspected), no meditation-practice variable, scale totals only; PHLMS awareness and acceptance correlate r = 0.12.

quantities.name: r_acceptance_dass_total
quantities.baseline: awareness r = -0.06; simple slope of awareness on DASS: -1.09 points/SD at low acceptance, +1.86 at high

quantities.name: r_phlms_awareness_ders_lack_of_awareness
quantities.source: reanalysis/out/a1.txt and the overlap check in NOTES.md
quantities.baseline: PHLMS awareness vs DERS clarity -0.52; PHLMS acceptance vs DERS non-acceptance -0.53; awareness vs DERS total -0.52, -0.43 with the awareness subscale removed

our_assessment.why: My own analysis, recorded as a draft because the authors' paper is not yet findable and their claims are unknown. The harms-literature hypothesis (heightened awareness without equanimity -> distress) gets no support here, but the sample is not selected for meditation practice, n is modest, and the design is cross-sectional, so this is weak evidence against a mechanism that, if real, would show up in practitioners. The more durable point is for whoever reads the eventual paper: PHLMS awareness and DERS 'lack of awareness'/'clarity', and PHLMS acceptance and DERS 'non-acceptance', partly measure the same constructs, so any mediation 'mindfulness -> emotion regulation -> outcome' on these scales is inflated by measurement overlap.

claims.statement: Out-of-sample test in 815 meditators (pre-registered, reanalysis/PLAN_ireland.md): the 'awareness without equanimity' interaction (TMS curiosity x decentering on DASS-21 total) has the hypothesised negative sign but is not significant on the pre-registered scale (-0.70 DASS points, HC3 p = .35); on the pre-stated log(1+DASS) robustness scale it is (-0.109, p = .010).
claims.scope: Zenodo 19701724 (Ireland, submitted), N = 955 adult meditators, 815 complete cases; parcel-level composites only, no practice variables; curiosity mapped to 'awareness', decentering to 'equanimity' BEFORE fitting -- the TMS is not the PHLMS of c1, so c1 and c2 test the same idea with different instruments.

quantities.name: interaction_curiosity_x_decentering_on_dass_total
quantities.unit: DASS-21 total points per SD x SD (HC3)
quantities.baseline: p = 0.350; log(1+DASS) scale -0.109, p = 0.010; c1 (non-meditators, PHLMS) +0.08, p = .30

quantities.name: partial_association_curiosity_with_dass_given_decentering
quantities.unit: DASS-21 points per SD of curiosity
quantities.baseline: zero-order r(curiosity, DASS) = -0.018: a suppression pattern (r(curiosity, decentering) = 0.451); shrinks to +0.82 (p = .13) when MAAS is added (exploratory)

quantities.name: r_maas_curiosity
quantities.baseline: MAAS-decentering 0.320; MAAS-DASS -0.554; two 'mindfulness' scales sharing no variance

our_assessment.why: Pre-registered and run as planned, known-answer check passed (planted -3.0 recovered as -3.02; planted 0 as +0.02). By the pre-stated primary test H1 is NOT supported, as I predicted; but the sign is the hypothesised one, the log-scale robustness check is significant, and curiosity -- unrelated to distress on its own -- carries MORE distress once decentering is held fixed, most steeply when decentering is low (simple slopes +3.37 vs +1.97). That is the shape the harms literature describes (open attention to experience without the capacity to stand back from it), seen weakly, scale-dependently, and not robust to adding MAAS. Together with c1, where the interaction had the OPPOSITE sign in non-meditators, the honest summary is: no clean evidence for the mechanism, a hint in practitioners only. The robust, citable finding is the construct one: MAAS and TMS curiosity correlate exactly 0.000, so 'mindfulness' predicts distress strongly or not at all depending on which instrument is read -- the dataset author's own thesis, confirmed on their data.

relations.why: Goldberg et al. and schlosser2019 locate meditation harms early and in a minority; this tests one proposed mechanism (awareness without acceptance) on independent data.

open_questions: Find the Antunes, Chiodelli & Jesus paper when it appears and compare their model with c1 and with the construct-overlap caveat.

PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-10-17 (c2): a practitioner sample with distress exists (Ireland, Zenodo 19701724) but has DASS, not harms (MRAES); the interaction is weak and scale-dependent there. A practitioner sample with BOTH equanimity-type and harm measures is still missing; vandam2025 (OSF 3mn9y) may be it.
